points.text: f(2x + 6) = f(2(x + 3)): a translation of 3 units to the left, then a horizontal squeeze by a factor of 2.
Factor out the 2 before reading the shift: 2x + 6 = 2(x + 3), so the inside change is x + 3, which shifts the graph left by 3 - reading the 6 directly would give the wrong shift.

items.prompt: Rewrite f(2x + 6) in the form f(2(x + c)) and state the horizontal translation it shows.

points.text: Vertical asymptote x = 2; horizontal asymptote y = 1.
The denominator is zero at x = 2, so the curve shoots up the line x = 2 and never touches it. As x grows large, 1/(x - 2) shrinks toward 0, so the curve flattens onto y = 0 + 1 = 1.

items.prompt: State the equations of the vertical and horizontal asymptotes of y = 1/(x - 2) + 1.

points.text: Sets dy/dx = 0 and solves to x = 1 and x = 3
